about.title: El Monte Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A space heater that catches fire in a Valley Boulevard apartment. A car seat buckle that gives way on Lower Azusa Road. A power tool that kicks back on a job off Peck Road. Defective products reach El Monte households the same way they reach the rest of Los Angeles County — through big-box stores, online orders, and the dealerships and parts counters along the I-10 corridor. California handles these cases differently from ordinary negligence claims. Under strict liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can each be held responsible. The single most important thing you can do is keep the product itself — do not throw it away, return it, or let anyone repair it. We handle product liability claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why El Monte Residents Choose Us

items.title: Strict liability works in your favor
items.desc: California generally does not require you to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused your injury. We build cases around that standard.

items.title: Every link in the chain may answer
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the El Monte retailer who sold the item can all be liable under California law. We identify each responsible party rather than stopping at one.

items.title: Preserving the evidence early
items.desc: The product itself is the heart of a defect case. We advise quickly on storing it safely before anything is discarded, returned, or altered.

items.question: My airbag or seatbelt failed in a crash on the I-10 through El Monte. Is that a product liability case?
items.answer: It can be, and it may sit alongside an ordinary car accident claim. El Monte recorded 539 injury collisions in 2025, and some involve components that did not perform as designed. If a restraint, tire, or brake part failed, the manufacturer or supplier may be strictly liable regardless of who caused the crash. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until an attorney has reviewed it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Generally, no. California's strict liability rule focuses on whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and whether that defect caused your injury. Whether the maker was careless is usually not the question. That said, each case has its own facts, and we can tell you how the rule applies to yours.

items.question: I already threw the packaging away. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. The product itself matters most, so hold onto it and photograph it from every angle. Receipts, order confirmations, and photos of the injury also help establish where and when you bought it. We can assess what evidence remains and what can be reconstructed.
